Cervical Vertebrae|.text: Cervical vertebrae have a small body, reflecting the fact that they carry the least amount of body weight.
Cervical Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|.text: Cervical vertebrae usually have a bifid (Y-shaped) spinous process.
Cervical Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.text: Cervical vertebrae have a small body, reflecting the fact that they carry the least amount of body weight.
Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.text: Cervical vertebrae usually have a bifid (Y-shaped) spinous process.
Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.text: The first cervical (C1) vertebra is also called the atlas, because this is the vertebra that supports the skull on top of the vertebral column (in Greek mythology, Atlas was the god who supported the heavens on his shoulders).
Cervical Vertebrae|atlas.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|axis.text: Cervical vertebrae have a small body, reflecting the fact that they carry the least amount of body weight.
Cervical Vertebrae|axis.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|axis.text: Cervical vertebrae usually have a bifid (Y-shaped) spinous process.
Cervical Vertebrae|axis.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Cervical Vertebrae|axis.text: The axis resembles typical cervical vertebrae in most respects, but is easily distinguished by the dens (odontoid process), a bony projection that extends upward from the vertebral body.
Cervical Vertebrae|axis.label: 7.3 Cervical Vertebrae

Thoracic Vertebrae|.text: The characteristic feature for a typical midthoracic vertebra is the spinous process, which is long and has a pronounced downward angle that causes it to overlap the next inferior vertebra.
Thoracic Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Thoracic Vertebrae

Thoracic Vertebrae|.text: The superior articular facets of thoracic vertebrae face posteriorly and the inferior facets face anteriorly.
Thoracic Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Thoracic Vertebrae

Lumbar Vertebrae|.text: They have short transverse processes and a short, blunt spinous process that projects posteriorly.
Lumbar Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Lumbar Vertebrae

Lumbar Vertebrae|.text: The articular processes are large, with the superior process facing medially and the inferior facing laterally.
Lumbar Vertebrae|.label: 7.3 Lumbar Vertebrae

Sacrum and Coccyx|sacrum.text: It is formed by the fusion of five sacral vertebrae, a process that does not begin until after the age of 20.
Sacrum and Coccyx|sacrum.label: 7.3 Sacrum and Coccyx

Sacrum and Coccyx|sacrum.text: On the anterior surface of the older adult sacrum, the lines of vertebral fusion can be seen as four transverse ridges.
Sacrum and Coccyx|sacrum.label: 7.3 Sacrum and Coccyx

Intervertebral Disc|.text: Each disc is anchored to the bodies of its adjacent vertebrae, thus strongly uniting these.
Intervertebral Disc|.label: 7.3 Intervertebral Disc

Intervertebral Disc|.text: The discs also provide padding between vertebrae during weight bearing.
Intervertebral Disc|.label: 7.3 Intervertebral Disc

overview.text: It consists of a sequence of vertebrae (singular = vertebra), each of which is separated and united by an intervertebral disc.
overview.label: 7.3 The Vertebral Column

overview.text: Together, the vertebrae and intervertebral discs form the vertebral column.
overview.label: 7.3 The Vertebral Column

overview.text: It is a flexible column that supports the head, neck, and body and allows for their movements.
overview.label: 7.3 The Vertebral Column
